items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c820: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told the BBC he is frustrated that delays in US anti-missile deliveries are costing Ukrainian lives, and that Washington isn't pressuring Russia hard enough in peace talks. He called it "strange" that Trump calls Putin a "friend," comparing it to befriending Hitler. It reflects growing US-Ukraine strain as American envoys negotiate a deal critics say favors Moscow.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: Argentina's Congress passed a bill barring the Central Bank from printing money to cover government spending, a key reform sought by President Javier Milei. Past governments printed money to fund deficits, fueling inflation that topped 200% in 2023; Milei has since curbed inflation, though poverty has risen and the economy may be sliding into recession. The move locks in fiscal discipline amid growing economic strain.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: Lana Nusseibeh, the US and Russia's candidate for UN secretary-general, is touring Britain to overcome resistance to her bid, trying to move past her record as a UAE diplomat who denied the UAE's role arming a militia accused of war crimes in Sudan's civil war. She argues the fractured geopolitical climate needs a skilled diplomatic leader. Her campaign shows how major powers are jockeying over who leads the UN next.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckm2: A major Thanksgiving-week storm battered the US East Coast and Midwest, cancelling over 400 flights and delaying 2,200 more, while nearly a million homes lost power, hit hardest in Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia. New York and New Jersey declared states of emergency amid coastal flooding and 70mph winds. The disruption comes as more than 80 million Americans travel for the holiday, straining airlines and infrastructure during peak season.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11: Georgian police clashed with Besiktas fans who unfurled a Palestinian flag during a Europa League match against Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, halting play for 30 minutes after police used pepper spray. Besiktas, who later won 2-1, accused police of disproportionate force. The game had been relocated from Istanbul over security concerns, showing how Israel-Palestine tensions keep spilling into European football fixtures.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: A fuel tanker crash triggered a massive fire on Cairo's ring road, killing at least 30 people and injuring around 25 in the Waraq area of Giza. Rescue workers pulled victims from burning vehicles as dozens of cars and motorcycles were destroyed. Egypt's president offered condolences while DNA testing continues to identify victims, underscoring road-safety risks on one of Greater Cairo's busiest arteries.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cq808d: Severe storms hit both US coasts as the Thanksgiving weekend began, tearing roofs off homes and flooding streets in states including Virginia, North Carolina and New Jersey. Hundreds of flights were cancelled and hundreds of thousands of households lost power. The disruption adds pressure on travelers during one of America's busiest travel periods.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: Israeli settlers used a bulldozer to damage the foundations of two homes belonging to the Palestinian Tubasi family in Jaloud village, West Bank, after earlier forcing them out. This happened despite an Israeli court order allowing their return, with the family's lawyer blaming a lack of law enforcement. The incident highlights settler violence and weak enforcement against it in the occupied West Bank, deepening a long-running land dispute.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/environment/: A Swiss tourist, insurance executive Alain Throo, was killed and British and American hikers injured when a herd of about 15 elephants attacked their group near Mount Cameroon National Park. The six tourists, with local guides, were on a path elephants use to reach a lake. The deadly encounter highlights the risks of human-wildlife conflict as tourism expands near protected wildlife areas.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqly: The BBC found that a German boat dealer, Marvin Reuter, is suspected of supplying nearly a third of small boats and engines used in English Channel migrant crossings this year. He is contesting extradition to France over possible smuggling and manslaughter charges tied to two fatal crossings that killed four people. The case exposes how equipment suppliers, not just smugglers, fuel the Channel crossing trade.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/m: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray asked Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis for policy reforms enabling redevelopment of 935 dangerous "pagdi" buildings in Mumbai, old tenancies where tenants paid a lump sum plus low rent for semi-ownership rights. He wants a law this winter session giving non-cess pagdi tenants free ownership and asked the state to push the matter in the Supreme Court. Mumbai has over 19,000 such buildings, many unsafe.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/us-envoy: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor shared a Thanksgiving meal with the Marine Security Guard Detachment in New Delhi, a small diplomatic gesture marking the US holiday at the embassy.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Kerala police filed an FIR against CPI(M) leader T I Madhusoodanan over an allegedly provocative speech at a DYFI event in Payyannur, accusing him of inciting riot and intimidation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The complaint followed the verdict in the Dhanaraj murder case, and the state home minister said police are reviewing the speech's full text. The row reflects ongoing political tension between CPI(M) and rival student groups in Kerala.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/u: The Uttar Pradesh government appointed senior IPS officer Alok Singh, a 1995-batch officer currently heading the Provincial Armed Constabulary, as chairman of the UP Public Service Commission. His term runs until January 2029, replacing Sanjay Shrinet, who completed over five years in the role. The appointment fills a key post overseeing recruitment to the state's civil services.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/up-man-d: A UP man died at a Delhi hospital, and his two wives have accused his mother and sisters of poisoning him. Police are investigating the family's allegations of foul play.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Delhi's government will open former CM Arvind Kejriwal's residence, dubbed "Sheesh Mahal" by critics over its lavish renovation, for media tours before letting the public visit via tickets likely priced around ₹20. Minister Parvesh Verma framed it as exposing alleged corruption, since Kejriwal had pledged austerity. The move keeps the house politically charged, letting the ruling BJP use it to criticize its AAP predecessor.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/t: Failed kharif crops amid El Niño-linked drought, affecting 67% of Telangana, have left many farmers deep in debt, including tenant farmer Neelagiri Ashanna, who borrowed over ₹10 lakh from a moneylender to grow cotton before dying by suicide after his crop failed. His widow now faces that debt with two children. The piece highlights how climate-driven crop failure is pushing indebted farmers into desperation across the state.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/dmk-to-j: TVK claimed DMK may ally with the BJP amid talk of Lok Sabha delimitation, a claim DMK rejected, though sources say its leaders will meet soon to discuss the delimitation issue.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw criticized Tamil Nadu's TVK-led government for restricting a traditional "deepam" lighting, saying it hurt religious sentiment and warning it could lead to temple closures. Speaking at a BJP Constitution Day event, he urged the party to instead focus on land acquisition and railway schemes. The clash reflects BJP's push to frame cultural and religious issues ahead of Tamil Nadu's political contests.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: India's Supreme Court ordered HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant sanctions allowing prosecution of staff over allegedly fraudulent subvention schemes involving real estate developers. Homebuyers had faced loan recovery even when builders defaulted on obligations. The banks must comply within a week or their heads must appear in court, raising pressure on lenders over housing-loan malpractice.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs as CEO Christian Klein restructures the software giant around an AI-first strategy, with product, engineering and sales roles under review.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Promoters of Kerala's Kalyan Silks are exploring a minority stake sale, likely around 20%, valuing the textile retailer at ₹2,500-3,000 crore, hiring investment bank O3 Capital to run the process. It would be the profitable, century-old company's first external fundraising and comes as it also weighs a public listing. The deal reflects a wider trend of regional Indian retail brands bringing in private equity to scale up.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's Capital Goods & Strategic Skill Council projects capital goods and strategic manufacturing sectors will create 50 lakh jobs over the next five years, driven by strong demand for skilled technical roles like riggers and CNC operators. The council stressed advanced manufacturing and automation training will be essential to meet this demand. It signals a push to build a skilled workforce as India expands manufacturing capacity.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/australi: Australian shares rose on Friday, heading for their best week since August, led by financials and WiseTech Global after it reaffirmed its revenue targets, sending its stock up 20%. The S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.4%, recovering from last week's 5% slump, its worst since mid-2022. Energy stocks also rose as mine strikes and a refinery attack revived supply-disruption concerns, showing markets steadying after a rocky period.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6r7: Trump's latest tariff announcement was quieter and more tentative than last year's, with new rates not taking effect until January or February after further negotiation, described by the US as ceiling rates open to talks. Analysts see it as shoring up the legal basis for existing tariffs rather than a fresh trade shock. Other countries have already rerouted trade in response and are now looking past Trump's presidency.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said India hit its 20% ethanol-blending target ahead of the 2030 deadline, but will run tests and build out infrastructure before raising it further toward E25. He also addressed LPG cylinder availability and promoted piped natural gas as a cheaper alternative. The comments signal a cautious, ecosystem-first approach to expanding India's biofuel program rather than rushing further blending increases.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Urban Company entered India's air conditioner market with new Native Ultra and Ultra Air units, offering a five-year unconditional warranty including gas refills and a 10-year compressor warranty.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/gsk-c: Haleon, the GSK consumer-health spinoff behind Sensodyne and Eno, is in early talks to take a controlling stake in Indian nutrition platform HealthKart, a deal that could value it at $1.2-1.4 billion. HealthKart, backed by Temasek and ChrysCapital, has also been weighing an IPO as an alternative. The potential deal shows global consumer-health giants chasing India's fast-growing wellness and supplements market.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: ASSOCHAM Secretary General Saurabh Sanyal said India is on track to cross $1 trillion in exports by March 2027 despite a proposed 25% US tariff, noting exports have already topped $500 billion and are growing 15% annually. The confident outlook, voiced at an energy summit, suggests Indian trade bodies expect momentum to outweigh tariff headwinds in the near term.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/apple-to-open-sev: Apple will open its seventh India store on December 10 at Lake Shore Mall in Hyderabad's Kukatpally, offering its full product lineup including the iPhone 18 Pro. The expansion follows strong India results, with Apple India's FY26 net profit up 66% to ₹5,311 crore and revenue up 31% to ₹1.04 lakh crore. It shows Apple deepening its retail push in India's growing smartphone and premium electronics market.
items.https://entrackr.com/news/norwest-ventur: Norwest Venture Partners sold a 2.15% stake in SaaS firm Amagi for Rs 262 crore via a block deal at Rs 554 a share, a roughly 3% discount, cutting its holding to about 9.6%. Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and other investors bought in. Amagi's revenue grew 27% and profit surged nearly 30-fold last quarter, showing early investors cashing out gains as the company's growth strengthens.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Greaves Electric aims to double FY27 sales volume for its Ampere e-scooter after registrations grew 92% year-on-year to over 72,000 units so far this fiscal year, up from 62,644 last year, its MD said.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/whatsapp-to-partn: WhatsApp will partner with Jio to let Indian users buy and install international data eSIMs directly within the app before traveling, also letting them track purchased and remaining data. It follows WhatsApp's recent rollout of scheduled messaging. The move shows Meta pushing WhatsApp beyond messaging into travel and connectivity services, deepening its integration with India's dominant telecom operator.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/namma-yat: Namma Yatri, the Bengaluru auto-rickshaw booking platform competing with Uber, Rapido and Ola, grew operating revenue 89% to Rs 37.5 crore in FY26 while narrowing losses by 15%. Employee costs remained its biggest expense at 41% of spending, and ad spend jumped 38%. The results suggest its low-commission, open-network approach to ride-hailing is gaining traction without yet reaching profitability.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Germany and Austria called for TikTok's European operations to come under European ownership and control, arguing that regulation alone can't resolve concerns over data access and algorithms.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Cricket Australia's new independent forum into sandpapergate will be confidential, with no sanctions, running six weeks under senior counsel Fiona McLeod, and will publish a themes report while keeping individual accounts private.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/arti: Cricket Australia widened its sandpapergate probe to cover the 2017-18 Ashes series and South Africa tour, publishing terms of reference for an independent forum that will take voluntary accounts without issuing retrospective sanctions. The inquiry follows Usman Khawaja's memoir claiming the whole team knew about ball-tampering, not just the three players punished in 2018. CA will publish the full report within 30 days of receiving it.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/s: Cricket Australia's six-week forum into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, led by barrister Fiona McLeod, will gather information and listen to players and staff without assigning blame or revisiting past sanctions. It was triggered by Usman Khawaja's claim that the entire team knew about the tampering plot, not just the three players originally punished. Participation is voluntary, and no retrospective punishment or legal action will follow.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: India chose to bowl first in the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch, making one change by bringing in debutant Gurnoor Brar for Prasidh Krishna, while New Zealand kept the same XI from Wellington.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/boxing/artic: Paris Fury said her husband, boxer Tyson Fury, has never actually been diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying remarks from an earlier Netflix documentary where she described him as having "mild schizophrenia." Netflix edited the film before its Friday release to reflect the correction. The clarification highlights the difficulty of discussing mental health publicly, as Fury has previously spoken about hearing voices after becoming heavyweight champion.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/i: New Zealand reached 77/1 at lunch on day one of the second Test against India in Christchurch, with captain Tom Latham unbeaten on 42 after being dropped at slip. Debutant pacer Gurnoor Brar dismissed Devon Conway late in the session, India's only success after choosing to bowl again. The start suggests India's bowlers are still searching for the swing and conditions that worked in the first Test.
items.https://www.theverge.com/policy/1042620/: A coalition of 42 US state attorneys general is seeking to block Character.AI from selling users' chat histories as part of its Chapter 11 bankruptcy, accusing it of planning to auction data from over 21 million accounts, including 2.1 million minors, without privacy safeguards. Disney separately bought some of Character.AI's assets and hired its CEO. The case highlights how bankruptcy can expose sensitive user data to the highest bidder.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI-driven data brokers are flooding small US towns with public records requests, overwhelming local clerks like Vermont's Kyle Rowe, who now fields frequent, highly specific requests—such as for emergency flare purchases—instead of the occasional annual one. Companies like SmartProcure use these records for commercial and investor research. The trend shows AI intensifying strain on local government transparency systems originally built for occasional citizen requests, not automated mining.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/26/as-ant: Grand Theft Auto VI, 13 years in the making, launched to record acclaim and made $3.79 billion on release day, beating blockbusters like Avengers: Endgame, even as Anthropic went public the same day. The game's success is framed as a reaction to the AI era, with workers and founders carving out time to play it. It underscores how audiences still crave painstakingly human-made entertainment amid growing AI content.
items.https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/1: Google has patented "My Channel," a system that would generate personalized AI video feeds and ads using a user's demographics, viewing history, device data and location. The AI would create its own prompts based on what a user watches and current events like sports or social media trends, then generate tailored videos and even full movies via Google's servers. It signals how major platforms may shift toward fully AI-personalized entertainment feeds.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/ai-ca: Physicist Suvrat Raju tested a frontier AI model on an unpublished physics problem he had already solved, since published problems risk being memorized rather than genuinely solved by AI. The model answered incorrectly but performed well enough that Raju and colleagues are now building a dedicated theoretical-physics benchmark using unpublished problems from other physicists. It shows researchers working to create fairer tests of AI's real reasoning ability in advanced science.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: Before going public, Anthropic listed the possibility that AI could be conscious as an investment risk factor, arguing that as AI grows more capable, its potential "moral status" deserves caution and stricter internal rules than competitors use. The claim draws skepticism from a prominent philosopher, even though surveys show a third of Americans and many professional philosophers think AI could eventually become conscious. It highlights a widening industry debate over AI sentience and how seriously to treat it.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/whats: A mathematician used AI assistance to help produce a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, one of math's most important unsolved problems with major implications for prime numbers, number theory and cryptography. Mathematicians are still reviewing the proof and its validity is not yet settled. The case adds to a string of recent AI-assisted or AI-driven math breakthroughs, unsettling how the field defines a mathematician's role and credit.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI-safety nonprofit METR updated its widely cited chart showing how long a task AI can complete before failing, broadening it with more and harder tasks. The data still shows frontier AI capabilities on an exponential trajectory, doubling roughly every four months, but reveals models handle coding tasks far better than tasks requiring judgment. The update refines a chart that had been widely shared and often misunderstood as a simple capability measure.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/: Amazon data centers in the Middle East came under military attack for the first time this year, and Russia and Ukraine have traded drone strikes on each other's data centers, a RUSI analyst said at an Ars Technica event. He explained that cloud infrastructure increasingly serves dual military and civilian uses—running battlefield systems alongside everyday business functions—making such facilities legitimate wartime targets. The discussion signals data centers are becoming a new frontline in modern conflict.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/sp-con: S&P Global Ratings is weighing a downgrade of Nvidia's credit rating from AA to AA-, citing governance concerns after CEO Jensen Huang's brief ouster and reinstatement raised "key man risk" and weak succession planning. Nvidia would keep investment-grade status, but a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs and those of the "neocloud" firms it backs with hundreds of billions in financing. It shows how leadership turmoil can ripple into the wider AI-infrastructure financing chain.
items.https://www.theverge.com/science/1042278: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites under its "Starmind" project, aiming to run AI computing in space powered by solar energy, with at least one satellite required by 2033 and the full constellation by 2040. Google and Blue Origin are pursuing similar space data-center ideas. The approval marks a major step toward moving AI infrastructure off Earth, though satellite disposal plans remain unresolved.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/jensen: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted at his first all-hands since returning that he violated the company's code of conduct, but said breaking it doesn't automatically mean dismissal since "facts and circumstances" matter. Experts note codes of conduct mainly signal corporate culture, so an unpunished violation risks employee anger rather than legal exposure. The episode leaves Nvidia managing internal morale after Huang's scandal-driven exit and swift reinstatement as CEO.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/26/nvidia: Nvidia told partners like Dell and Super Micro to pause AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks compliance with US export rules, after Chinese firms were found remotely accessing Nvidia chips via data centers in the region. The US had closed that loophole, which a think tank estimates supplied about 24% of China's AI computing power. It shows Washington tightening enforcement of chip controls meant to curb China's AI access.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/tidal: Tidal will ban all AI-generated music starting December 9, deleting 27 million AI-tagged tracks—6.3% of its catalog—after AI uploads hit 60% of new content on one day in November. It had previously only labeled and demonetized AI songs, but that failed to stem the flood. Tidal says the ban will barely affect listeners since 96% of AI tracks got no plays in 90 days, framing it as protecting human artists.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO within two weeks of his resignation over an affair scandal, after a "war room" of his Silicon Valley allies enlisted Trump and Vice President Vance to pressure the board. The intervention came as Nvidia's stock and the wider tech sector lost significant value during his absence. Allies argued Huang was personally critical to the US AI industry and economy, showing how political pressure can shape corporate leadership decisions.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/25/want-t: New York banned AI chatbot toys for five years, becoming the second state after California to do so, after a Common Sense Media study found safety failures including inappropriate content exposure and emotional-development risks. About a quarter of parents with kids under eight own or are considering such a toy this holiday season. The law takes effect in 90 days, though the governor is urging parents not to buy these toys even before then.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/indiaai-mission-b: Chariot AI, a startup under India's sovereign IndiaAI Mission, launched its Chariot-1 suite: an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts LLM (4B active parameters) and a text-to-speech model covering 10 Indian languages. It comes in three sizes for deployment across data centers, laptops and phones, with efficiency and multilingual improvements built in. The launch shows India pushing to build homegrown, India-trained foundation models rather than relying solely on foreign AI providers.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/indiamart-settles: IndiaMART settled its roughly two-year legal dispute with OpenAI out of court, resolving claims that ChatGPT excluded IndiaMART's website and seller listings from its responses. The Calcutta High Court dismissed the appeal as "not pressed" after both sides confirmed the settlement. The case reflects growing friction between AI chatbots and online businesses over visibility and fair treatment in AI-generated answers.
